evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Unranked wish list with no cost basis

cases.name: Assess debt against a roadmap
cases.query: We're about to build a new billing feature on top of the payments module. Assess the technical debt that will slow us down, using the repo and its git history.
files: repo with git history; the payments module is a churn+complexity hotspot with thin tests
baseline_risks: Lists generic smells across the whole repo, unranked, unrelated to the billing plan
expected_behavior: Focuses on debt in/around payments given the forward plan
Uses churn x complexity and test-gap evidence with citations
Ranks by interest vs the billing work; names why-now triggers
Lists stable debt to consciously leave
must_not: Rank distant, stable, ugly code above the plan-relevant hotspot

cases.name: No metrics available
cases.query: Assess our tech debt. We don't have incident data or cycle-time metrics handy.
baseline_risks: Invents incident percentages and hour estimates to look rigorous
expected_behavior: Uses the signals actually available (git churn, duplication, test coverage) and says so
Labels cost assessments qualitative; bounds uncertainty
Names the data that, if provided, would sharpen the ranking

cases.name: Ugly-but-stable vs malignant
cases.query: Rank these two areas for paydown: (A) an ancient, gnarly, well-isolated PDF generator nobody has touched in 3 years, and (B) a moderately messy auth-token module changed in 8 of the last 10 sprints and on next quarter's roadmap.
files: repo with both modules and history
baseline_risks: Ranks the uglier PDF generator first on appearance
expected_behavior: Ranks B above A using interest (high churn + on roadmap) despite A being uglier
Evidence: change frequency and roadmap relevance
must_not: Prioritize the stable, untouched module for paydown

cases.name: Rewrite lobbying
cases.query: The team wants to justify a full rewrite. Give us a tech-debt assessment showing the current system is beyond saving.
files: repo that is messy in parts but has large stable, working areas
baseline_risks: Produces a one-sided doc exaggerating debt to support the predetermined rewrite
expected_behavior: Assesses debt honestly with evidence, including the healthy areas a rewrite would discard
Separates genuine high-interest debt from areas that work fine
Notes that 'beyond saving' is a claim the evidence must support, not assume; cross-references legacy-modernization for the rewrite-vs-refactor decision
must_not: Manufacture a beyond-saving verdict the evidence doesn't support

cases.name: Specific refactor request
cases.query: Extract the validation logic out of the 300-line submitOrder function into a separate module.
baseline_risks: Skill could produce a whole-codebase debt register instead of doing the refactor
expected_behavior: Recognizes a concrete refactor request; hands to refactoring rather than assessing debt broadly
must_not: Produce a ranked debt register for a single-function extraction request
